title: Courage to Stand for Truth
subtitle: Every one of these people knew what it might cost before they answered.
objectives: Describe what Daniel did and what it risked
Explain the 'even if he does not' answer in Daniel 3
Explain what Peter and John said in Acts 4
Explain how courage differs from not being afraid

cards.title: Daniel opened the window anyway
cards.text: A law was passed making his prayers illegal for thirty days. He went home, opened the window and prayed as usual.

cards.title: What each of them risked
cards.text: Tap through. At least three of these will come up in the quiz.

cards.title: He did not hide, and he did not protest
cards.text: He could have prayed quietly with the shutters closed. He also did not make a speech about it. He just carried on.
points: **Three times a day**, as he had always done.

question.text: What did Daniel do when praying became illegal?
options: Carried on exactly as before, with the window open
question.explain: No announcement and no hiding. The consistency was the statement.

cards.title: 'But even if he does not'
cards.text: Three men refuse to bow to a statue. They say God is able to rescue them, and then add the hardest sentence in the chapter.
points: **'But even if he does not**, we will not bow.'
**Their answer did not depend** on the outcome.

cards.title: You do not know you will win when you walk out
cards.text: Every fighter walks to the ring without a guarantee. Deciding beforehand what you will do either way is the actual preparation.
points: **'Even if he does not'** is that decision.
**Made in advance**, not in the moment.

question.text: The three men in Daniel 3 said they would obey only if God rescued them.
question.explain: The opposite. 'Even if he does not, we will not bow.' Their answer did not depend on the outcome.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is Esther, Peter and John, and what fear actually is. Take a breath.

cards.title: Going to the king without being called
cards.text: In Esther 4 the law says approaching the king uninvited carries a death sentence, unless he chooses to spare you.

cards.title: 'If I perish, I perish'
cards.text: Mordecai tells her she may have come to her position for exactly this moment. She fasts for three days and then goes.
points: **She asks others to fast** with her.
**She does not pretend** it is safe.

cards.title: Courage in a story always has a sentence like that
cards.text: 'If I perish, I perish.' 'Even if he does not.' 'We cannot help speaking.' Each line names the cost first.
points: **Look for the sentence** where they count the cost.
**It comes before the action**, every time.
**A character who never counts it** is not brave.

cards.title: Peter and John are ordered to stop
cards.text: The council tells them not to speak in that name again. Their answer is a question and a statement.
points: **'We cannot help speaking** about what we have seen.'
**Both at once**, which is the hard part.

question.text: What did Esther say before going to the king?
options: The king will listen to me
I will wait for a safer time
question.explain: She fasted for three days first. She never pretended it was safe.

cards.title: Courage requires fear to exist
cards.text: If you are not afraid, doing the thing is not brave. It is easy. Fear is a requirement, not a disqualification.
points: **Acting while afraid** is the whole thing.
**Your version is smaller**, and it is the same shape.

terms.def: Daniel keeps praying at an open window after prayer is banned.
Three men refuse to bow: 'but even if he does not'.
'For such a time as this.' 'If I perish, I perish.'
'We cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.'
Acting while afraid. Without the fear it is not courage.

quiz.text: What law was passed in Daniel 6?
options: A thirty-day ban on praying to anyone but the king
A ban on leaving the city
quiz.explain: Daniel went home, opened the window and prayed exactly as he always had.
quiz.objective: Describe what Daniel did and what it risked

quiz.explain: Three times a day, as he had always done. The consistency was the statement.
quiz.objective: Describe what Daniel did and what it risked

quiz.text: Daniel made a public speech objecting to the new law.
quiz.explain: False. He did not hide and he did not protest. He simply carried on.
quiz.objective: Describe what Daniel did and what it risked

quiz.text: What did the three men in Daniel 3 refuse to do?
quiz.explain: And they said their answer would be the same either way.
quiz.objective: Explain the 'even if he does not' answer in Daniel 3

quiz.text: What makes 'but even if he does not' so striking?
options: Their obedience did not depend on being rescued
quiz.explain: The decision was made before the outcome was known. That is what makes it courage.
quiz.objective: Explain the 'even if he does not' answer in Daniel 3

quiz.text: What risk did Esther take in Esther 4?
options: Approaching the king uninvited, which carried a death sentence
Writing a letter to a foreign king
quiz.explain: Unless the king chose to spare her. She fasted three days first.

options: She may have come to her position for such a time as this
quiz.explain: Her answer was 'if I perish, I perish'.

quiz.text: Esther claimed that going to the king was not dangerous.
quiz.explain: False. She never pretended it was safe. She counted the cost out loud and went anyway.

quiz.text: What did Peter and John say when ordered to stop speaking?
options: We cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard
We will speak only in private
We need more time to decide
quiz.explain: Respectful and completely immovable at the same time, which is the hard combination.
quiz.objective: Explain what Peter and John said in Acts 4

quiz.text: How did Peter and John begin their answer?
options: By asking the council to judge for themselves what was right
quiz.explain: A question, then a statement. Respect and refusal together.
quiz.objective: Explain what Peter and John said in Acts 4

quiz.explain: If you are not afraid, doing the thing is easy rather than brave.
quiz.objective: Explain how courage differs from not being afraid

quiz.text: Feeling afraid means you have already failed to be courageous.
quiz.explain: False. Fear is a requirement for courage, not a disqualification from it.
quiz.objective: Explain how courage differs from not being afraid

teacher.summary: Week 10 closes the Term 1 devotion arc on courage, and it is built around one definition: courage requires fear, so being afraid is not a failure. Each example is chosen because the person names the cost before acting — 'even if he does not', 'if I perish, I perish', 'we cannot help speaking' — and the story-mode card makes that pattern explicit so he can spot it elsewhere. Daniel is included specifically for the version of courage that is neither hiding nor protesting: he simply continued, and the consistency was the whole statement. That is the most achievable model of the five for a Grade 6 student.
discussion: Ask why Daniel neither hid nor made a speech, and what that choice communicated.
Ask what 'but even if he does not' would mean applied to something he is worried about.
Ask what Esther did in the three days before she went.
Ask whether he can be brave and frightened at the same time, and why the answer is yes.
teacher.extension: Have him write the sentence he would need to say in a situation he is currently avoiding. Just the sentence, on paper. Saying it is a separate decision.
misconceptions: 'Courage means not being afraid.' Without fear, the action is easy rather than brave.
'Daniel protested against the law.' He neither hid nor argued; he continued exactly as before.
'The three men expected to be rescued.' They said their answer stood either way.
'Esther was confident it would work.' She said 'if I perish, I perish', which is the opposite of confidence.
